newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait bourse dips in "healthy" correction-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait bourse dips in "healthy" correction-dealers.

text.p: Trade levels on the Kuwait Stock Exchange eased on the week to Wednesday after riding high for several weeks in what dealers called a healthy correction.
"This is a normal correction phase. This is healthy. It ends concern about prices on the long-run," said Nasser Bou-Resli, a protfolio manager at Coast Investment.
"If the market keeps rising something bad could come next. This is normal," said Jassem al-Saad, a private dealer.
Traded value fell 8.0 percent to 329.8 million dinars ($1.1 billion), a daily average of 65.9 million dinars. The exchange operates for two and a half hours five days a week.
Volume eased 26.4 percent to 1.195 billion shares, a daily average of 239 million shares. Gainers led loosers 32-17 in the week, while eight were non-movers.
The index, which rose 1.2 percent to 1,877.9 this week, fell 1.4 percent from record 1,905.2 points registered on Sunday.

Dealers attributed the upward trend that lasted for several weeks to capital flows from neighbouring states, strong mid-year results by listed firms, lack of other local investment vehicles and strong economic indicators.

Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest through mutual funds ran by local firms.
Kuwait is considering opening trade for foreign investors.
Commercial Bank, Investment Projects, Bahrain International Bank, United Realty, Gulf Bank and Fujairah Cement were among the most traded shares.

Banks were the most active sector by value with 42 percent, foreign firms shares followed with 14.1 percent and investment firms with 13.9 percent. Foreign firms were the most active by volume with 30 percent.
"People now are buying bank shares after talk of privatisation plans and blue chips to benefit from year end dividend," said Bou-Resli.
